newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX April COB electricity expires up, PV down.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX April COB electricity expires up, PV down.

text.p: NYMEX April electricity futures expired mixed Tuesday amid steady to higher spot cash market prices in the western U.S. and news about power plant outages in the Southwest.

April California-Oregon Border (COB) futures expired up 28 cents at $11.15 a megawatt hour (MWh) after posting a high of $11.45. May COB finished up 30 cents at $10.25. Deferred COB months ended flat 25 cents higher.

April PV futures went off the board lower in a late sell off, down five cents at $14.56 after hitting a high of $15.00. May PV finished up 25 cents at $14.55. Other active PV contracts ended 10 to 27 cents higher.

The April power contracts were given a jolt early today on news that production of the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Palo Verde (PV) nuclear generating station in Arizona was cut to 61 percent to repair its low pressure feedwater system.
The power cutback was brief, and Palo Verde unit 1 was ramping toward full power by late morning.
"The market got a little spooked by Palo Verde," said one futures trader.
Later, Southern California Edison said restart of the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant has been delayed by another week to April 1 from Thursday.
Peak, firm electricity prices for day-ahead delivery at COB was steady at $11.00-12.00, while those at PV climbed 75 cents to $14.75-15.75.
While spot supplies in Southwest appeared tight, power availability in the Northwest is expected to grow with increasing runoffs into the region's hydroelectric dams.

Because its output cannot compete with the plentiful supply of cheap hydroelelctricity, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington will be shut early Thursday, several weeks earlier than planned for refueling and maintenance.

Some of the vast amount of hydropower could move to the Southwest whenever Bonneville Power Administration could ramp up the Pacific Intertie by 1,050 MW to 6,250 MW. The intertie has been held at 5,200 MW due to problems with maintenance at a 500 kilovolt portion of the system in Oregon.
Market sources said they are uncertain about the direction for the May contracts because of the usual mild temperatures and light energy usage expected during that month.

In the Northwest, temperatures were forecast to average about 15 degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the northeast section for the rest of the week, while readings along the coast would run normal to two degrees Fahrenheit above normal.
In the Southwest, temperatures would run above normal across the region with the northeastern area averaging 12 degrees above seasonal norms.
